correctness.rationale: In the displayed complete DFA, the hidden map is the square of the visible map and hence commutes with it. The states 2,0,1 are reached by ε,a,aa; b separates 2 and 0, and ε separates 1 from both. The projected acceptance sequence is 1,1,0,1,0,…, with three distinct residuals at lengths 0,1,2 (lengths 0 and 1 are distinguished by one more a). Hidden closures are exactly {1,2},{0},{1}, so the overlap persists before minimization. For the lower bound, commute every hidden letter past the visible letters to recognize the projection on the original state set with hidden-reachability finals. Full two-state projected complexity then forces a transposition or a constant, as identity reaches only the start. For the transposition, the only commuting maps are identity and the transposition, yielding singleton closures or the whole set. For a constant with distinct start d and image c, infinitude and minimality force c projected-final and d not projected-final. Every commuting hidden map fixes c and cannot send d to c, so all hidden maps are identities. The one-state case is immediate. This covers any nonempty hidden alphabet. Independent bounded replay at /workspace/branches/993b2af2-76e4-4355-bd94-c3aa05179b8c/independent_projection_check.py (output independent_projection_check.txt) checked the witness and all 128 labeled two-state binary DFAs: 80 commute, six have infinite minimal unary projection of size two, and none of those six overlaps. This is corroboration, not the many-hidden-letter proof. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.

value.rationale: This exact minimum answers the natural equality question for commutative projection: retaining all minimal states, even for an infinite unary projection, does not require disjoint hidden closures. The smallest obstruction separates these two properties while preserving full minimal size; the proof excludes smaller obstructions for every number of hidden letters, not just the enumerated alphabet. The claim is a minimal witness, not a general classification.
